THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.t: THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.short: Ama sells tomatoes to feed Grandma. Madam Darkoa, 53yrs witch, sells tomatoes that never spoil. Each tomato is a trapped destiny.
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.long: At Kaneshie Market, poor Ama must stop Madam Darkoa, a 53yrs market witch whose tomatoes glow green and steal destiny. 99 victims already, Ama will be number 100.
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.full:
1. NARRATOR: Kaneshie Market, 4am, dark, cold, only torch lights. Ama Mensah, 22 years, beautiful, hardworking, very poor tomato seller, carries heavy basket on head from Agbogbloshie. She walks alone to feed her blind grandmother Grandma Esi and her brother Kofi who is trotro driver but jobless.

2. AMA MENSAH: (sweating) Grandma Esi, today I will sell all my tomatoes by God's grace. I am tired of poverty. Kofi trotro no work, you blind, I am the only one. But I will not steal, I will not do juju. I will work hard with clean hands.

3. GRANDMA ESI: (65 years, blind but sees spirits, holding stick) My granddaughter Ama, my spirit is not comfortable today. I am blind with eyes but I see with spirit. Not all red is tomato. Not all shining market is clean. Some traders sell more than goods. They sell destiny. Be careful in Kaneshie today, my child.

4. NARRATOR: Same market, same row, Madam Darkoa, 53 years, The Market Witch, strange woman. No one knows where she comes from, no family. She sells reddest, biggest, beautiful tomatoes. Her stall always dark even afternoon. Her tomatoes glow green at night and never spoil for 2 months. Customers start leaving Ama.

5. AMA MENSAH: (crying small) Why customers no dey buy from me today? My tomatoes fresh from Agbogbloshie this morning. I wake 4am. But everyone goes to Madam Darkoa. Her tomatoes never spoil? How? Something is wrong.

6. AFIA: (21 years, Ama jealous best friend) Ama, make I try buy one from Madam Darkoa and see. Maybe her own get chemical? She says her own stays 2 months without fridge.

7. GRANDMA ESI: (touches Afia tomato, hand shakes, shouts loud) AHHHH! This is not tomato! This is destiny! This is human star! She is stealing people's stars! Afia, where you buy this evil thing? Throw it away!

8. GRANDMA ESI: (blind eyes turning white) That woman is a market witch! In 1973, she was cursed by Nana Okomfo for using 3 children for money rituals at Tano River. The curse said she will never die, she will live by stealing other people's destiny. When you eat her tomato, she exchanges your good luck for her bad luck. Your market will die, your womb will close, your husband will leave you, your hair will fall, your money will vanish.

9. AFIA: (crying, hair falling) Too late Grandma Esi! I ate yesterday! I made stew! My boyfriend broke up this morning, my hair falling when I comb, my small savings GHC 200 disappeared! I am finished!

10. AMA MENSAH: (angry, brave) I must confront her! Tonight midnight at Kaneshie when market empty! No one will steal my destiny!

11. NARRATOR: Midnight, 12:05am, empty Kaneshie Market, dogs barking far, only wind. Ama hides behind Queen Yaa stall. She sees Madam Darkoa sitting alone in middle of her dark stall, holding one tomato floating in air, with green lightning inside, chanting.

12. MADAM DARKOA: (voice like many women inside one) Give me your market... give me your marriage... give me your children... give me your womb... give me your money... I give you tomatoes...

13. MADAM DARKOA: (turns, yellow glowing eyes like poster, smiles) You small girl... you want to know my secret? Come closer. Buy one tomato. Just one. One tomato for your whole future.

14. NARRATOR: Ama runs away with fear, heart beating like drum. She runs straight to Makola to Mallam Musah, 80 years old mallam, who knows about market witches.

15. MALLAM MUSAH: (looks at Ama palm with small mirror) Eii, Ama Mensah, your destiny star already dim. You touched her stall last week when you borrowed knife. She started taking small small. Your customers reducing, body itching at night, dreaming of old woman? That is her hand. Take black soap and white handkerchief blessed at Mecca. Don't eat anything in market for 7 days. Don't take money with left hand. Bring me one glowing tomato at 12 midnight on 7th day.

16. AMA MENSAH: (kneeling) I will do it Mallam. I will fast, I will pray. Save me and my grandmother.

17. NARRATOR: 7th day, midnight, heavy rain, thunder. Ama with white handkerchief over head, steals one tomato from Madam Darkoa basket when Madam Darkoa goes to urinate behind stall. Tomato heavy like stone, cold like ice block, inside Ama hears baby crying, woman crying, man shouting for help.

18. AMA MENSAH: Eiii! This tomato heavy! Cold! I hear baby crying inside! Mallam, what is this? (cuts with knife) Blood comes out, not water! Fresh human blood!

19. MALLAM MUSAH: (puts tomato inside fire with incense, fire turns green, many faces appear) Ama, look! Each tomato is trapped destiny! This woman crying, she was tomato seller at Makola, lost all market. This young girl can't marry for 5 years. This man now mad at Lapaz. Madam Darkoa trapped 99 destinies. You will be number 100 and she will become young again, 22 years like you, and you will become old like her and die!

20. NARRATOR: Meanwhile Kofi, Ama brother, 24 years, trotro driver, jobless, greedy, jealous of Ama small success, hears about Madam Darkoa quick money from friends at drinking spot.

21. KOFI: (goes to Madam Darkoa at midnight) Madam Darkoa, make me rich. I hear you give money quick. I will bring you my sister. She is beautiful, her star bright.

22. MADAM DARKOA: (laughs, gives GHC 5000 cash instantly) Bring Ama hair from her sponge, and her pant from drying line. And bring her picture. I will make you rich in one night.

23. KOFI: (steals Ama pant from drying line at 2am) Forgive me sister, I need money for trotro.

24. AMA MENSAH: (dreaming, woman with green hands strangling her inside her own stall) Ah! Leave me! Madam Darkoa, leave me! (wakes sweating, green hand marks on neck)

25. MALLAM MUSAH: (serious) Ama, only one way left. No more time. Kofi betrayed you. She has your pant. You must sell cursed tomato back to Madam Darkoa on Tuesday market day, when market fullest, when queen mother Queen Yaa is there. If she eats her own trap, power will break.

26. NARRATOR: Tuesday, Kaneshie full like Christmas, thousands market women. Queen Yaa, 45 years, market queen mother, inspecting stalls. Ama with fear, holding cursed tomato wrapped in white handkerchief blessed by Mallam Musah, goes to Madam Darkoa stall.

27. AMA MENSAH: (voice shaking but brave) Madam Darkoa, good morning. I want to sell you tomato. Very fresh. From my farm. Better than yours. Sweeter. Taste and see.

28. MADAM DARKOA: (laughs loud, all market women look) You small girl want to sell tomato to tomato seller? Okay, give me. Let me taste your poor tomato. (takes it, bites) AHHH! AHHH! WHAT HAVE YOU DONE!

29. NARRATOR: Green lightning explodes from Madam Darkoa mouth, eyes, hands! Throat glows green, skin cracks like old rotten tomato, blue Kente turns black. All trapped destinies fly out as bright green lights and return to owners. Market women who poor suddenly get customers. Girl who couldn't marry for 7 years gets proposal same day.

30. MADAM DARKOA: If I go down, you go down with me! AMA MENSAH: I reject you in Jesus name and Allah name! Kaneshie market is for hard work, not witchcraft! GRANDMA ESI: (blind grandmother appears, pours black soap water) Return to where you came from, witch! GBOOOM! Madam Darkoa melts into pile of rotten tomatoes, green smoke to sky. Only her stall burns with green fire. QUEEN YAA: From today, Madam Darkoa spot given to Ama Mensah for bravery! We pray every Monday! KOFI: (kneels) Ama, forgive me, I was greedy. AMA MENSAH: I forgive you brother, but return GHC 5000 to Mallam Musah for cleansing. NARRATOR: One month later, Ama biggest tomato business in Kaneshie and Agbogbloshie. Mr Joseph, rich businessman, gives her cold store. She marries Mr Joseph son, kind man. At night, when Ama closes stall, sometimes she still sees one green tomato glowing under Madam Darkoa old table... She never touches it.
 
THE END.

 MORAL: Not every shining business clean. Hard work with small profit better than quick money that steals future.

ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.t: ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT
ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.short: Akokrom village near Kumasi cursed - No one can sleep for 7 months! Children cry, farmers farm with no rest. Chief promises 2 fat goats & gold dust. Kwaku Ananse comes with a clever trick that shocks everyone. Will silence bring sleep back? Ananse story from Ashanti Region, Ghana.
ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.long: Long ago in Akokrom village, Ashanti Region near Kumasi, Ghana, a strange curse falls - no one can sleep at night. Not children, not old men, not even goats. For 7 months, eyes stay open till morning. The chief calls wise men, the fetish priest says Asaase Yaa Mother Earth is angry because youth make noise every night with drums and fights. Kwaku Ananse the clever spider man hears about 2 fat goats and gold dust reward and walks to Akokrom. With just a drum, palm wine, and silence from 7pm to 5am, Ananse tricks the whole village to sleep again. An Ashanti folktale about respect, peace, and the power of silence. Ghana Ananse story by ZEENATFLIX, inspired by @zeenat69.sonkowa.
ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.full:
1. Long, long ago, in the Ashanti Region, not far from Kumasi, there was a village called Akokrom.

2. Akokrom was a happy village, but they had one big problem. No one could sleep at night. Not because of noise. Not because of mosquitoes. But because the village was cursed to always be awake.

3. Every night, when the sun set, the people of Akokrom would lie on their mats, close their eyes, but sleep would not come. Their eyes stayed open till morning. Children cried, old men were tired, farmers went to farm without rest.

4. The problem started 7 months ago. Before that, Akokrom was famous for deep sleep. But after the new youth leader, BRONI KYEKYEKU, said "We will not sleep, we will enjoy night life," everything changed.

5. Every night there was Boboobo, there was drumming, there was fight at the palm wine bar. The night became louder than day. The old gods of night became angry.

6. The chief, NANA KYEI, called all the wise men. NANA KYEI said, "Who can bring sleep back to our village? My own eyes have not closed for 21 nights. I am 50 years old and I am tired."

7. OKOMFO TANO, the fetish priest, sacrificed a fowl. OKOMFO TANO said, "The earth spirit, Asaase Yaa, is angry. You have stolen the night's peace."

8. One day, KWAKU ANANSE, the clever spider man, heard about it in his village. Ananse was not from Akokrom, but he heard that NANA KYEI promised 2 fat goats and a bag of gold dust to anyone who could bring sleep.

9. Ananse smiled. His jealous wife AHENEMAA told him, "This one is not about trick, my husband." Ananse said, "Sleep? That is easy! I will trick sleep and bring it here."

10. Ananse packed his small bag, took his walking stick, and walked to Akokrom. The journey took one day. When he arrived, the village looked tired. Even the goats were awake and crying! Babies were awake with red eyes.

11. Ananse went to NANA KYEI. "Nana, I can bring sleep back in 3 days. But I need one night alone in the village square, and everyone must obey me."

12. NANA KYEI agreed and gave Ananse a stool. That night, Ananse went to the square with a big drum. He started drumming. Gbo gbo gbo! He sang: "Sleep, sleep, come to Akokrom, We are tired, we want to sleep."

13. All the villagers came out, tired and angry. "We don't want drum! We want sleep!" Ananse stopped drumming and laughed.

14. Then Ananse did something clever. He brought a pot of palm wine and poured it on the ground. "This is for Asaase Yaa, Mother Earth," he shouted. "We have offended the earth, that is why she took our sleep!"

15. Ananse told them, "For years, you have been making noise at night, fighting, playing drums till midnight. You never let the earth rest. So the earth also took your rest! Every night you insult the night."

16. The old people nodded. It was true. Akokrom had become a noisy village. Young boys fought over girls till 2am. Women argued at the borehole till 1am. All because of BRONI KYEKYEKU.

17. Ananse said, "Tonight, no one will talk. No one will drum. No fire will burn. We will all sit in silence from 7pm to 5am. We will show respect to the night. If anyone makes noise, I will leave." BRONI KYEKYEKU was angry but NANA KYEI forced him to keep quiet.

18. BRONI KYEKYEKU laughed, "Silence cannot bring sleep. We tried herbs!" Ananse replied, "Noise has taken your sleep, silence will bring it back."

19. That night, for the first time in many months, Akokrom was quiet. No talking. No drumming. No fighting. Only the crickets and frogs. Even the dogs stopped barking because Ananse gave them bones.

20. At 7:30pm, Ananse told everyone to lie on mats in the square and close eyes. He told a story slowly, in a very low voice: "Once upon a time, the moon was sleeping... and Asaase Yaa was watching..."

21. His voice was so slow, so calm. Little EFYA POKUAA, the 6-year-old girl, yawned... and closed her eyes... and slept! Krr... EFYA POKUAA slept first! Then her mother slept. Then NANA KYEI slept.

22. One by one, the whole village fell into deep, sweet sleep. Krr krr - snoring filled the air! Even BRONI KYEKYEKU slept with mouth open! Even Ananse himself slept, with one leg up!

23. At 5am, the cock crowed. Akokrom woke up happy! They had slept after 7 months! EFYA POKUAA was jumping, women were singing.

24. They carried KWAKU ANANSE on their shoulders. "Ananse is wise! Ananse has brought sleep!"

25. NANA KYEI gave him the 2 fat goats and a bag of gold dust as promised. But BRONI KYEKYEKU asked, "Ananse, what magic did you use? Did OKOMFO TANO help you?"

26. But Ananse, being Ananse, laughed and said, "I did not bring sleep with magic. Sleep was always here. You just chased it away with noise and worry. When you respect the night, the night will respect you."

27. Ananse showed them his secret - he had not drummed loudly, he had whispered. He had not brought medicine, he had brought silence. OKOMFO TANO nodded, "The earth is happy now."

28. Ananse took his goats and went home to his wife AHENEMAA, but he left one advice: "Every night, after 8pm, let your village sleep. No loud noise, no quarrel, no drum. Let children like EFYA POKUAA sleep early. Then sleep will never leave you again."

29. The people of Akokrom made a new law that day: From 8pm to 5am, no drumming, no fighting. And anyone who breaks it, like BRONI KYEKYEKU used to, will fetch water for the whole village.

30. And till today, the people of Akokrom sleep early and wake strong. They never forgot Ananse's wisdom and the names of NANA KYEI, EFYA POKUAA, and BRONI KYEKYEKU.

MORAL OF THE STORY: Respect the night and your body. Sleep is not bought with money, it comes with peace. If you make noise in the night, the night will take your sleep.

THE ABANDONED HUTS.short: Emmanuel returns from Accra after 15 years to see 3 abandoned huts no one dares enter. Old Papa Kwasi says Maame Serwaa vanished there 40 years ago. Villagers say she is a witch. That night Emmanuel hears singing from the huts...
THE ABANDONED HUTS.long: Maame Serwaa vanished 40 years ago from 3 huts at village edge. Everyone said she was a witch. Emmanuel, city boy from Accra, returns after 15 years and hears old Papa Kwasi's true story. That night singing comes from the huts... Emmanuel enters with torch and finds Maame Serwaa alive, not ghost. Why did she vanish? Papa Kwasi confesses he started witch rumor from jealousy. Beautiful Ghana village folktale about jealousy, kindness, and forgiveness. Watch till end - mist vanishing twist will shock you.
THE ABANDONED HUTS.full:
1. Emmanuel, handsome young man in white shirt and clean jeans, returns to his grandfather's village after 15 years in the city of Accra.

2. The villagers stare as he walks. "The city boy is back! Accra boy has returned!" they whisper. Emmanuel smiles but feels strange.

3. At the edge of the village, near the forest, he sees something strange - 3 old huts covered in thick bush, roofs broken, doors open. No footpath to them.

4. Children playing near shout, "Don't go! That is Maame Serwaa place! Abandoned huts!" They run away scared.

5. Emmanuel asks a woman, "Why are those huts abandoned?" The woman covers her mouth, "We don't talk about Maame Serwaa. Come away."

6. That evening, an old man with a walking stick appears. This is PAPA KWASI, 87 years old, the oldest man in the village and the only one who knows the true story.

7. Papa Kwasi says, "You want to know about those 3 huts, city boy? Sit. I will tell you, but you city boys don't believe old people."

8. 40 years ago, there lived a kindest old woman called MAAME SERWAA. She had 3 huts - one for cooking, one for sleeping, one for her powerful herbs. She helped pregnant women and healed sick children for free.

9. Everyone in the village loved Maame Serwaa. If your child cried at night, you went to her. If your wife was pregnant, you went to her. She never asked for money.

10. But other women became jealous. "Why does everyone love Maame Serwaa? She is too kind, there must be something inside her! She is a witch!"

11. One rainy night with heavy thunder, Maame Serwaa went to her 3 huts singing a lullaby. The whole village heard her singing. Morning time, she was gone.

12. Her wrapper was on the ground, but no body, no footprints. Like mist took her. For 40 years, no one saw her again. The huts became cursed.

13. Since then, anyone who entered heard crying at night. In 1998, a young man entered and ran mad for 3 days shouting "Old woman! Old woman!" So they abandoned it completely.

14. Emmanuel laughs loudly. "Papa Kwasi! You old people and your stories! Witch? Vanishing? This is 2026!"

15. Papa Kwasi gets very angry and hits his stick on the ground. "You city boys think you know everything because you wear white shirt! You know nothing!"

16. That night, Emmanuel cannot sleep in his grandfather's house. The village is too quiet. Then he hears it - an old woman singing from the direction of the 3 huts. The same lullaby Papa Kwasi sang.

17. His heart beats fast. He takes his torch and follows the sound, pushing through thick bush, mosquitoes biting.

18. First hut - empty, only spider webs and broken stool. Second hut - her old mortar and pestle still there, as if she just left yesterday.

19. Third hut - he freezes. Inside, back to him, stands an old woman in clean wrapper, singing the same lullaby she used to sing for children 40 years ago. Not old wrapper, clean one.

20. She turns slowly. It is MAAME SERWAA. She is not a scary ghost. Her eyes are full of tears, not anger. Her face is kindest in the world.

21. "You are Kwasi's grandson," she whispers with sweet voice. "You have his eyes. Same eyes that lied about me."

22. Emmanuel drops his torch, shaking. "You... you are alive? For 40 years we thought you were dead! Or a ghost!"

23. Maame Serwaa smiles. "I never died, my son. I vanished. There is a difference. I walked into the mist to save them."

24. Flashback - that rainy night 40 years ago. Jealous women came with cutlasses and fire to burn her 3 huts, shouting "Witch! Witch!" Maame Serwaa heard them.

25. She did not run from fear - she ran from love. She knew if she stayed, the village would kill each other. Her kindness would cause blood. So she walked into forest mist, singing loudly so they would think spirits took her. She left her wrapper on purpose.

26. "For 40 years I lived deep in forest," she tells Emmanuel. "Every night I came to leave herbs for sick children at edge of huts. They called me witch because I was kind, so I became mist, so kindness would not cause hate."

27. Behind Emmanuel, Papa Kwasi appears with his stick, crying for first time in 40 years. Behind him, all villagers holding lanterns, scared.

28. Papa Kwasi falls on knees. "Maame Serwaa! Forgive me! I started the rumor!" All villagers gasp. Papa Kwasi confesses - he was young and jealous because everyone respected Maame Serwaa more than him, the elder. He told people she is witch.

29. Maame Serwaa does not get angry. She touches Papa Kwasi's head gently. "My son, I forgave you the night I left. 40 years ago."

30. She walks towards her huts. Thick white mist rolls from forest. She turns one last time to Emmanuel. "Don't let them abandon kindness again." She steps into mist and slowly vanishes - not scary, but beautiful, like mother going to sleep. Her wrapper floats and lands in Emmanuel's hands. One month later, Emmanuel uses his city money to rebuild the 3 huts - Hut 1 Clinic, Hut 2 Story Hut where Papa Kwasi tells true story, Hut 3 Herb Hut carved MAAME SERWAA - THE WOMAN WHO VANISHED TO SAVE US. At night, you still hear her singing, but now children smile and sing along.

MORAL: Some secrets vanish in mist, but kindness never does. Don't call kind people witches.

MY HUSBAND IS A SNAKE.short: Sandra, poor waitress, marries Frederick, handsome billionaire in one week. At midnight she finds giant python on bed of dollars with his voice. He did money ritual.
MY HUSBAND IS A SNAKE.long: Poor waitress Sandra from Kumasi marries billionaire Frederick in East Legon after one week. One rule: Never wake me at midnight. At 12AM she touches cold scales - her husband is giant python on bed of dollars. Pastor James reveals he must sacrifice wife and child to Python Temple. Sandra is pregnant with moving snake inside. Full moon is coming.
MY HUSBAND IS A SNAKE.full:
1. In East Legon, Accra, Sandra worked as a waitress. 24 years old, beautiful, but broke. Her mother MAMA NGOZI sold pure water on street to pay rent.

2. One night, a black Range Rover stopped at the restaurant. A man stepped out - very handsome, fair, tall, jawline sharp like movie star, suit worth 20,000 cedis. This is FREDERICK, 30 years.

3. Every girl in restaurant stared. Frederick pointed at Sandra. "You. Bring my drink." His voice was deep and rich.

4. From that night, Sandra's life changed. Next day iPhone 15 Pro Max delivered. Then human hair wigs, red hot dresses, gold chains, 20,000 cedis momo every week.

5. Frederick said, "I have never loved any woman like this. Marry me next week." Sandra's best friend CHIDI shouted, "Girl, you have hammered!"

6. MAMA NGOZI was scared. "Sandra, one week marriage? You don't know his family, his village, his past! Fast love is fast tears!"

7. But Sandra was blinded by luxury. Wedding happened in one week. No one from Frederick's family came except FREDERICK'S MOTHER, who whispered to him, "Don't show her the midnight form."

8. After wedding, they moved to luxury penthouse overlooking Accra. Bed covered with dollar stacks, Rolex watches, diamond earrings. Richest house Sandra ever saw.

9. That night, Frederick gave her one rule. "Sandra, never wake me at midnight. Never look at me at midnight. I have a skin condition that makes me scary."

10. Sandra agreed. First 2 days were paradise. Driver EMEKA drove her, house girl BLESSING served her. Rich life.

11. At 12:00 AM on third night, Sandra woke to use bathroom. She touched her husband's body to cross him. It was cold. Scaly. Like fish scales.

12. She turned on light, shaking. Her handsome fair husband was gone. On bed was giant python, thick as a man, eyes glowing yellow, lying on money. Shadow on wall exactly like python shadow.

13. She screamed loud. The python spoke with Frederick's voice. "Sandra... why did you wake me? Why did you break rule?"

14. In seconds, it turned back to Frederick. Naked, scales disappearing into fair skin, tongue splitting back to normal.

15. "You're a snake! You're a python!" Sandra cried, running to corner. Frederick cleaned himself calmly. "I made covenant with Python Temple. They made me rich. Every midnight I become what I truly am. If you tell anyone, you will die."

16. Sandra ran to PASTOR JAMES next morning, fire pastor who sees spirits. Pastor James shouted, "This man did money ritual! Python gave him wealth, but he must sacrifice his wife after one year and his first child to snake! His two former wives disappeared!"

17. House girl BLESSING confirmed, crying. "Madam, the woman before you shouted 'snake' at midnight. Next morning, I only saw blood on bedsheet. Madam, run!"

18. Sandra followed Frederick's driver EMEKA on Thursday. He drove deep into bush to BABA SNAKE shrine, powerful juju man at Python Temple with snakes everywhere.

19. Hidden behind tree, Sandra heard BABA SNAKE tell Frederick, "You brought fine new wife. Good. But remember, after she gives birth, you must bring baby for python to swallow, or you will become python forever and lose all your money."

20. Sandra touched her stomach - she was already pregnant. But pregnancy was not normal. Two weeks pregnant, belly was like five months. Something moved inside like snake coiling.

21. At midnight, Frederick in python form would come and lick her belly, whispering with forked tongue, "My python prince... soon you will come..."

22. Sandra tried to escape. She packed Ghana-Must-Go bag with dollars. But at 11:50 PM, all doors locked spiritually. Windows closed by themselves.

23. Frederick started transforming in front of her - handsome face cracking into scales, eyes turning yellow, tongue splitting into two. "Where are you going, my wife? You are carrying my heir. You cannot leave."

24. That was when MAMA NGOZI and PASTOR JAMES broke door with holy water and anointing oil, shouting, "In name of Jesus! Snake spirit, leave this house!"

25. When holy water touched Frederick, he screamed like 100 snakes. Giant python shadow on wall behind him started burning, like your poster burning.

26. BABA SNAKE appeared in spirit, angry, with live pythons around neck. "Frederick! You allowed pastor into your house! You broke covenant! Now you will lose everything!"

27. Instantly, money on bed vanished. Rolex watches vanished. Penthouse shook like earthquake. Dollars turned to snake skins.

28. Frederick, half-man half-python, looked at Sandra with yellow eyes and said his last words before disappearing into mist. "Sandra... even if you run... the baby inside you is already python. It will come out on full moon..."

29. Outside, full moon rose over Accra, big and red. Sandra's belly moved violently, something inside pushing like it wanted to slither out. BLESSING shouted, "Madam, your stomach is moving!"

30. TO BE CONTINUED... Will Sandra give birth to human baby or python? Will Pastor James break money ritual before full moon? Will Frederick choose love or his billions? Part 2 coming - comment PYTHON if you want it!

MORAL LESSON: Not all that glitters is gold. Fast rich marriage can be snake pit. Ask about his midnight form before you say I do.

THE KAYAYO GIRL PART 1.short: Amina, 18, gets 7 A's in WASSCE, dreams to be lawyer. Her father sells her to 72-year-old Alhaji for 10 cows to pay bank debt. She runs midnight to Accra to become Kayayo.
THE KAYAYO GIRL PART 1.long: Amina Yakubu, pride of Gambaga with 7 A's, wants to be lawyer to stop forced marriage. Her father Alhassan owes bank GHC 25,000 and accepts 10 cows + GHC 30,000 from 72yr Alhaji Mumuni for her as 5th wife. Mother Fati gives her GHC 80 to run. She flees midnight to Abogbloshie to become Kayayo carrying yams to station. Meets sisters Mariam and Asana.
THE KAYAYO GIRL PART 1.full:
1. Amina Yakubu is the pride of Gambaga. 18 years old, beautiful, just finished Gambaga Girls SHS with 7 A's in WASSCE. Dream: become lawyer to stop forced marriage in the North.

2. Her father ALHASSAN YAKUBU, 55, yam farmer, owes bank GHC 25,000 for fertilizer loan. Bank says "Pay or we take your farm." He has no money.

3. Her mother FATI YAKUBU, 42, sells tuo zaafi, strong woman, not blind. She loves Amina's dream. "My daughter will be lawyer, not wife to old man."

4. One afternoon, rich man comes to compound. ALHAJI MUMUNI, 72 years old, from Nalerigu, very rich - many cows, shops, houses. 4 wives already. Big belly, white beard.

5. Outside their compound, 10 cows tied, mooing. Inside, Alhaji drops GHC 30,000 cash bag on floor. "Alhassan, give me your daughter Amina. Beautiful girl. I marry as 5th wife. I pay your debt plus 10 cows. She will not suffer."

6. Alhassan eyes shine seeing cows and money. "Alhaji! You have done well! Amina! Come! Your husband has come!"

7. Amina comes from farm carrying firewood on head, sweating. Sees old man. Shock. "Baaba! I am 18! I want university! This man older than my grandfather! 4 wives already!"

8. Fati cries, "Alhassan! Don't sell our daughter for money! She got 7 A's! She wants to be lawyer to help girls!"

9. Alhassan shouts, "7 A's will pay my bank debt? Will 7 A's feed us? Lawyer will feed us? She will marry Alhaji next week after Damba festival! No more school! Decision is final!"

10. Amina runs to her small room crying, holding her WASSCE result - 7 A's shining. "My dream is finished for 10 cows?"

11. That night, whole house sleeps. Fati enters quietly, gives Amina GHC 80 folded inside plastic and her WASSCE result. "Run, my daughter. Go to your brother YUSIF in Accra. Don't marry that old man. Go be Kayayo if you must, but be free."

12. 12 midnight, Amina packs small bag - one dress, one rubber slippers, and her WASSCE result paper. Barefoot, she runs through Gambaga bush, darkness, thorns cutting feet, to Nalerigu road.

13. On road, onion truck going to Accra stops. Driver: "Small girl, where are you going it's midnight?" Amina crying, "Abogbloshie. I want to be Kayayo."

14. Driver pities her, "Enter." She sits on onions, truck moving 14 hours through night, through Tamale, through Kintampo, to Accra. Tears dry on face.

15. Morning, she arrives ABOGBLOSHIE MARKET, Accra. Smoke, noise, shouting, thousands of northern girls with basins on heads shouting "Kaya! Kaya! Station! Station! Obaa where you dey go?"

16. Amina stands confused, holding bag, basin girls bumping her. She sees heavy yams, tomatoes, onions everywhere. No one knows her.

17. Suddenly, YUSIF, 24, her brother who works as truck loader at Abogbloshie, sees her. Shocked. "Amina! Father said you ran! Alhaji said if you don't come back he will take his cows and call police!"

18. Amina wipes tears, strong voice, "Let him take his cows. I will carry people's things to station than marry 72-year-old man for money. I will not be 5th wife."

19. Yusif sighs, gives her head-pad and old aluminum basin. "Here, we carry people's load to station, to trotro, to where they going. GHC 5, GHC 10 per load. At night we sleep on cardboard in front of stores. This is Kayayo life."

20. First load - Amina carries heavy yams from big truck to market woman's stall. Neck pains, basin heavy, feet burning on hot ground. Market woman insults, "Village girl, walk fast! You slow!"

21. Second load - tomatoes to trotro station. Third load - onions to woman's house. By noon, neck bleeds where pad sits, hands shake. She earns GHC 30 first day.

22. At night, she sleeps on cardboard in front of closed store with 20 other Kayayo girls, mosquitoes biting, no mosquito net, cold floor.

23. There she meets MARIAM ISSAH from Bawku, 19 years, loud, funny, also Kayayo. Mariam laughs, "Gambaga girl, don't cry! I also ran! My father wanted to marry me to 65-year-old man for 8 cows! Here we are sisters!"

24. And ASANA SALIFU from Walewale, 18 years, quiet, spiritual, always praying. Asana looks at Amina, "Amina, I dreamt you before you came. You are not Kayayo, you are lawyer. I saw you wearing black wig in London."

25. Amina laughs with tears, "Lawyer? I am carrying basin on head to station to station? How can Kayayo become lawyer?"

26. Asana says, "God shows me. Keep your WASSCE result safe inside plastic. Don't let water spoil it. That paper is your future."

27. From that day, Amina, Mariam, and Asana become 3 sisters - inseparable. Every day they carry people's things together from Abogbloshie Market to Accra Central Station.

28. Morning they wake 4am, tie head-pad, shout "Kaya!" Evening they count small money GHC 40, GHC 50, share one ball of kenkey and fish.

29. At night on cardboard, Amina brings out her WASSCE result under torchlight, reading 7 A's, while Mariam and Asana watch. "One day I will use this again," she whispers.

30. END OF PART 1... Will Alhaji Mumuni find Amina in Abogbloshie and force her back for his 10 cows? Will Amina survive Kayayo life with neck bleeding? Will her 7 A's ever become law wig? PART 2 - The Station Girl Becomes Lawyer - coming. Comment KAYAYO if you want Part 2.

MORAL: 10 cows cannot buy a dream. A daughter is not debt payment.

THE GOLDEN CALABASH PART 1.short: Ada, 19, poor girl in Imo State finds glowing golden calabash in river on full moon. Queen Zara inside makes her rich - but demands one child every year from her womb.
THE GOLDEN CALABASH PART 1.long: In Imo village, poor Ada fetches water at full moon and finds pure gold calabash glowing in river. Inside is Queen Zara, Goddess of Wealth trapped 200 years. Zara gives Ada millions daily, heals blind Mama Nneka. But price: one child every year on full moon. Ada gets pregnant without man, belly grows fast with coin sound. River priest Elder Okoro says calabash is cursed. Calabash stuck to her hands.
THE GOLDEN CALABASH PART 1.full:
1. In small village near river in Imo State, lived poor girl ADA, 19 years old, beautiful but very poor. Father died two years ago.

2. Her mother MAMA NNEKA, blind and very sick, always crying from hunger and blindness. Her elder brother CHINEDU, 26, lazy, always drinking palm wine and spending little money.

3. Ada was only one who worked. Fetched water, went to farm, cooked, wore same wrapper every day.

4. One night, no food in house. Mama Nneka crying. "Mama don't cry, I go river fetch water, maybe God help us," Ada said.

5. Full moon night, river calm and shining gold. At river bank, Ada saw something glowing inside water.

6. It was calabash, but not normal. Pure gold, shining with golden light, ancient designs on it, like in poster.

7. Ada looked around, no one there. She picked it. Moment she touched it, water started glowing with golden smoke.

8. She opened calabash. Inside gold dust, coins, and voice. Golden smoke came out and formed beautiful woman.

9. Woman skin was gold, hair like golden threads, teeth gold, many gold necklaces, but eyes yellow and evil. This was QUEEN ZARA.

10. "Thank you for freeing me, Ada. I trapped inside this calabash in river for 200 years. I am Goddess of Wealth. Whoever frees me, I make very rich," Queen Zara said with golden smile.

11. Ada scared but poor. "I only want money to buy medicine for my blind mother."

12. Queen Zara laughed, golden smoke entered Ada's wrapper. "Take me to your house. Keep me in room. Every morning shake me, I give you money."

13. Ada carried Golden Calabash home, hiding under wrapper.

14. Next morning, she shook it. Shaka shaka shaka... Money poured - gold coins, naira notes, dollars. Ten million naira!

15. Chinedu shouted, "Ada! Where you get this money? Did you steal?" Ada said, "I found golden calabash at river! It gives money!"

16. For one week, Ada shook calabash every morning. Money kept coming. Built new house, bought medicine, Mama Nneka started seeing again, Chinedu bought motorcycle, eating good food.

17. Whole village jealous. CHIEF OBI came, greedy village chief. "Ada, this calabash belongs to river, and river belongs to village. Give it to me. I am chief."

18. Ada refused. "River gave it to me. It chose me."

19. That night, Ada had strange dream. Queen Zara sitting on top of calabash in her room, now more real, more evil, smiling same as poster.

20. "Ada, you have enjoyed wealth. Now time to pay. Golden Calabash gives money, but wants a child every year," Zara said in dream.

21. Ada woke sweating. "A child? What child?" Queen Zara appeared physically in room with evil golden smile.

22. "Yes. Every year, on full moon night, you must give me child from your womb. I take child's spirit to remain powerful. If refuse, I take your mother back to blindness, then take her life."

23. Ada crying, "I am not even pregnant! I am virgin! You never told me about child!"

24. Queen Zara laughed and blew golden light into Ada's stomach. "You will be pregnant soon. Without man. My golden child."

25. Next morning, Ada stomach started growing fast. In two weeks, looked like three months. Villagers talking, "Ada pregnant without husband! She using children for money ritual with golden calabash!"

26. Her best friend AMARA betrayed her and told everyone, "She doing juju! She killed baby for gold!"

27. ELDER OKORO, old river priest who guards river, came to house and warned, "Ada, that calabash you took is cursed! 200 years ago, Queen Zara was wicked queen who killed babies to make gold. Gods punished her, locked spirit inside golden calabash, threw into river."

28. "Anyone who takes it will become rich, but she will demand one child every year until woman's womb empty," Elder Okoro said.

29. Ada crying, holding glowing calabash. Calabash now stuck to her hands with golden light. She cannot drop it, just like in poster. "Take it back! I don't want money anymore!"

30. Queen Zara angry voice from inside, "Too late, Ada. You already carrying my golden child. On next full moon, you will give birth. And I come to take it. Every year, one more, until your womb empty." Mama Nneka touched Ada stomach and screamed. Inside stomach, something kicked, but not like baby kicking. It sounded like coins shaking. Shaka shaka shaka... TO BE CONTINUED IN PART 2.

MORAL LESSON: Not all gold that glitters is gift. Some wealth demands womb.

SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.t: SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.short:
Choima, 22, from Onitsha is promised $500 house help job in Riyadh by agent Alhaja Kudirat.
She pays N350k and flies to Saudi, but madam seizes passport and phone.
No salary, 19 hours work daily. She was sold for $4000.
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.long:
Anambra girl Choima goes to Saudi for house help job to save her sick mother.
Agent collects N350k and sells her to Saudi madam for $4000. Passport and phone seized.
She works 5am to 1am, beaten, no salary for 6 months, locked in 48-degree heat.
She hides embassy number in her underwear and plans Friday escape with Fatima.
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.full:
1. CHOIMA, 22 years old, beautiful fair-skinned tall girl from Onitsha, Anambra State, with natural hair, sells zobo and meat pie at Onitsha Main Market to feed her four younger brothers and sisters after father died.

2. Her mother MAMA NNEKA very sick, leg swollen, hospital bill at Nnamdi Azikiwe Teaching Hospital is N450,000. Choima has no money, shop rent she cannot pay.

3. One afternoon, woman named ALHAJA KUDIRAT comes to market in black Lexus, wearing plenty gold, she is agent.

4. Alhaja looks at Choima and says, "My daughter, you are beautiful and hardworking. I have house help job for you in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Salary is $500 per month. Almost N800,000. In two years you can build house for your mother. Many Nigerian girls are there. They are enjoying."

5. Choima is scared. "Aunty, I saw on TikTok they beat house helps in Saudi. My friend from Asaba went and never came back."

6. Alhaja laughs. "That is Dubai and Libya, not Saudi. Saudi is good Islamic country. Very safe. My own daughter is there. She's student and drives Benz. Look." She shows video of Nigerian girl dancing in shopping mall in Riyadh.

7. Choima thinks about her mother lying on mat at home crying from pain, her brothers not in school, her shop rent. She says yes.

8. Alhaja asks for N350,000 for processing fee, visa, and ticket. Choima sells her mother's small wrapper shop and borrows money from her church to pay.

9. Alhaja takes her to Lagos to small house in Agege. For two weeks they train her how to clean toilet with hands, how to wear abaya, how to say "Naam Mama" which means "Yes Madam." No contract, no paper from NAPTIP, no meeting at embassy.

10. At Murtala Muhammed Airport Lagos, Alhaja collects Choima's passport. She says, "I will keep it safe. Your madam will give you new ID called Iqama when you arrive."

11. This is Choima's first time entering airplane. Lagos to Jeddah to Riyadh. Six hours. She wears new black abaya and cries inside plane.

12. At Riyadh Airport, Saudi woman picks her. Her name is MAMA UM KHALID, 50 years old, big, with seven children. Lives in big three-storey house.

13. In car, first thing Mama Um Khalid does is collect Choima's phone. "No phone. No Nigerian boyfriend. Only work."

14. Choima's room is not room. It is small store. No bed. Only thin mat on floor beside bags of rice. No fan.

15. First day real suffering starts. She wakes at 4am. Cooks breakfast for ten people. At 6am cleans five bedrooms and four toilets. At 11am washes clothes with hands. At 2pm cooks Kabsa rice for fifteen people because visitors come every day. At 5pm watches five noisy children. At midnight washes plates.

16. She works from 5am to 1am. Nineteen hours every day. No rest. Her feet swollen.

17. Her madam beats her with mop stick. She shouts, "Yalla! Yalla! Fast! You are slow! Donkey!" Choima cries inside toilet, same toilet she cleans. She remembers Onitsha Main Market where she was free.

18. After one month she asks, "Mama, please my salary? My mother sick in Anambra." Her madam shouts, "Salary after three months! I paid your agent $4,000 for you! You are my property now!"

19. That is when Choima understands. Alhaja did not find her job. Alhaja sold her for $4,000. She is not worker. She is like slave.

20. Three months pass. No salary. No phone. Her passport seized. House gate locked with camera. Her Iqama not done.

21. In sixth month, at night, madam's 20-year-old SON tries to enter her small store room while she sleeps on mat.

22. Choima screams and bites his hand and locks door. She reports to her madam. Instead of helping her, her madam beats her again. "You are seducing my son! You bad Nigerian girl!"

23. Her madam locks her outside house in 48-degree heat with no water for whole day.

24. Choima kneels outside in hot sun, wearing black abaya, sweating, looking at sky. She whispers, "God, I left Anambra to help my mother. Now I am slave in Saudi. Who will save me?"

25. Inside her underwear she hides small paper. She copied it from wall of airport toilet on day she arrived. It is number of Nigerian Embassy in Riyadh: +966 11 442 8624

26. But she has no phone to call.

27. That night, girl from next compound whispers through fence. Her name is FATIMA from Ibadan. "Choima, don't cry. Many Nigerian girls are here for one year with no salary. We will run to embassy together on Friday when madam goes to mosque..."

28. Choima holds fence, tears falling, but small hope comes for first time in six months.

29. Fatima whispers, "We have same embassy number. Many of us hiding it. Friday is only day they go to mosque. Gate man also goes."

30. Choima looks at hot Riyadh sky, holds embassy paper tight. One week to Friday. Will she escape or will madam catch her? 

MORAL: Before you travel for house help job, ask for NAPTIP paper and contract. Your passport is your life, don't give to agent.
